vanilla_raycast_fluid_none.conversion: A mixin method added to Level overrides BlockGetter's default clip (Mixin 0.8.5 has no injectors in interfaces): for a ClipContext of exactly that class with Fluid.NONE on a level whose class keeps Level.getFluidState, vanilla's own traversal (BlockGetter.traverseBlocks) runs with a step that makes every call of the original step in the same order except the fluid-state read (the fluid shape is asked for the empty fluid state, which NONE never looks at); every other clip calls BlockGetter's default method. The added method is an @Intrinsic soft implementation of BlockGetter.clip in a mixin of priority 1,000,000,000 (applied after every other mixin on Level): if any other mod has given Level its own clip, Mixin keeps theirs and skips ours (generic stand-down, proven offline in evidence/vanilla_raycast/yield-proof.json); the Valkyrien Skies yield below stays. 1.21.1: also stands down at run time (ClipFast.OTHER_CLIP) when another mixin is merged into BlockGetter's clip, its lambdas, traverseBlocks or clipWithInteractionOverride (@MixinMerged, e.g. an @Overwrite of the default method), or any injector handler is merged into BlockGetter; Level's clip is then BlockGetter's (modified) method for every context.
vanilla_raycast_fluid_none.license: Minecraft (Mojang): no-copy; the mixin and helper carry only our own logic (helper bons.furious.patch.vanilla_raycast.ClipFast)

yields.name: Valkyrien Skies
yields.why: Valkyrien Skies gives Level its own clip too (feature.clip_replace.MixinLevel: shipyard check, then its clipIncludeShips raycast through ships). Both mixins add Level.clip; only one method can exist, and Mixin skips the second with an overwrite-conflict warning, which would drop VS's ship raycasts. Our switch therefore stands down whenever VS's mixin is active (a yield never cancels VS's mixin: that only happens while our switch applies, i.e. without it).

yields.name: Radium
yields.why: Radium 0.13.1 (on by default; Radium reads config/lithium.properties) @Overwrites BlockGetter.clip, the default method every Level inherits, with its own raycast ("faster block accesses and more efficient fluid handling"). Our Level.clip would take NONE clips away from it; while Radium's option is on our switch steps aside and Level keeps Radium's clip. Without this line the run-time stand-down (ClipFast.OTHER_CLIP sees Radium's @MixinMerged on BlockGetter.clip) gives the same result one step later.
